title: Minestrone
subtitle: Italian vegetable and pasta soup
excerpt: A thick, hearty Italian vegetable soup packed with seasonal vegetables, cannellini beans, pasta, and a swirl of basil pesto. A soup that changes with the season and improves overnight.

recipe.sourceNotes: Minestrone (from the Italian minestra, meaning soup, and the augmentative -one, making it big soup) is the catch-all Italian term for a thick vegetable soup. There is no single canonical recipe: the dish is defined by the use of whatever vegetables are in season, combined with pasta or rice, often enriched with beans, and frequently finished with pesto. The soup is a feature of cucina povera, the Italian tradition of peasant cooking that makes the most of seasonal produce and storecupboard ingredients. Every region of Italy has its version: the Ligurian version uses basil pesto as a final flourish; the Venetian version uses rice; the Neapolitan version tends towards pasta and tomato. The common element is a soffritto base (onion, carrot, celery cooked in olive oil) and a long, slow simmer. The soup improves dramatically when kept overnight: the flavours meld and deepen, and the pasta becomes pleasantly soft.

recipeTools.notes: A very large saucepan or casserole.

content.text: Add the pasta in the final 10 minutes and watch carefully: pasta absorbs liquid and swells, and overcooked pasta makes the soup stodgy. If making ahead, cook the pasta separately and add it to bowls when serving. A Parmesan rind added to the pot while the soup simmers melts slowly and adds depth: save rinds in the freezer for this.

items.preparation: small pasta shapes such as ditalini or broken spaghetti
pesto, to serve; or a handful of fresh basil

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) and cook for 10 minutes until soft and beginning to colour. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the courgette, tinned tomatoes, stock, thyme, bay, and rosemary. Season. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 20 minutes. Add the cannellini beans and cook for 5 more minutes.

Add the pasta and cook for the time stated on the packet, usually 8 to 10 minutes. Remove the herb sprigs. Taste for seasoning. Serve in deep bowls with a spoonful of pesto and a drizzle of good olive oil.
